we found an NADP(+-)dependent enzyme activity in human liver nuclei that catalyzes the oxidation of corticosterone and other 11beta-hydoxysteroids.
we have found a new 11betaHST enzyme that uses NADP(+/+) as cofactor and is located in human liver nuclei.
we identified a novel 11beta-hyroxysteroid dehydrogeanase activity that utilizes NADP( +) as pyridine cofactor, and that is present in the nuclear fraction of human liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel NADP-dependent 11betaHSTD enzyme activity in human liver nuclei.

the characterization of a novel enzyme activity for 7- and 11-hydroxysteroidal dehydrogenases in human liver nuclear protein fractions that may be involved in the regulation of corticosteroid metabolism.

the discovery of a novel NADP(+-) dependent 11betaHDS enzyme in the nuclei of human liver that is distinct from 11betaHST1, but may be similar to Type 2 11betaHSTD, and that may be responsible for the conversion of cortisone to cortisol in the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a novel NADP(+/+)-dependent 7alpha/betahydroxysteroid oxidoreductase activity has been identified in the nuclear fraction of human liver.

the nuclear activity is a new NADP(+)/NAD(+)-dependent 7alpha/betahydroxysteroid/11betahydroxysteriod dehydrogenase, which is similar to 11betahydroxy steroid dehydrogenases Type 1 and Type 2, but is distinct from them.
the nuclear enzyme activity is a new 11betaHST, but that it is not a Type 1, 2 or 3 11betaHSTD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the liver contains two 11betaHDS, one in microsomes, 11betaHST1 and a second one in nuclei, which is a third 11betaHSTD.
human liver nuclei contain a novel 11beta-hydoxysteroid dehydrongenase with NADP(+)/NAD(+) cofactor preference that has a high affinity for corticosterone.
